Resolve a PAG to a representative MAG

Source: R/transform.R
mag_from_pag.Rd

Returns one MAG belonging to the Markov equivalence class represented by the PAG cg: a left inverse of mag_to_pag(), so mag_to_pag(mag_from_pag(pag)) recovers pag. Every circle mark left unresolved by the PAG is resolved to a tail or arrowhead following Zhang's construction (2008, Theorem 2): a circle opposite a fixed mark always becomes directed; an undirected edge (selection bias) is kept unchanged; the remaining all-circle edges form a chordal component, oriented into a DAG with no new unshielded colliders by Dor-Tarsi simplicial elimination.

Usage

mag_from_pag(cg)

Arguments

cg

A PAG created with cgraph().

Value

A MAG graph proxy.

References

Zhang J (2008). “On the completeness of orientation rules for causal discovery in the presence of latent confounders and selection bias.” Artificial Intelligence, 172(16-17), 1873–1896.

Dor D, Tarsi M (1992). “A simple algorithm to construct a consistent extension of a partially oriented graph.” Technical Report R-185, Cognitive Systems Laboratory, UCLA.

Examples

if (julia_ready()) {
  pag <- cgraph(A %o-o% B, B %o-o% C, class = "PAG")
  mag_from_pag(pag)
}
#> MAG with 3 nodes and 2 edges:
#>   nodes: A, B, C
#>   edges:
#>     B --> A, C --> B
